pagerduty: :rotating_light: Alert triggered — prod-inference-us-west | high 5xx rate (10.8%) across frontend gateways. Escalation policy: inference-slo -> oncall-engineering. Incident ID: INC-2026-4437
incident-bot: Bridge created: https://meet.example.com/reds/INC-2026-4437 (auto) — channel #incident-4437 created, recording enabled.
alice: I'm oncall — claiming. jumping into the bridge.
ben: Auto-escalated to me after 2m. if alice is on it, i'll standby for takeover if needed.
alice: thx. quick customer impact: some production text-gen requests returning 502/504s, customers seeing increased latency and a small % of failed requests. Not full outage but user-visible errors for ~5% of heavy tails.
carlos: attaching a short grep from gateway logs — looks like upstream inference pool returning 500s intermittently.
```
2026-03-15T14:03:21Z gateway-1 inference-proxy 500 "POST /v1/generate" 0.123s host=... instance=i-0a1b2c3d
2026-03-15T14:03:22Z gateway-2 inference-proxy 502 "POST /v1/generate" 0.456s host=... instance=i-0a1b2c3e
2026-03-15T14:03:24Z gateway-3 inference-proxy 504 "POST /v1/embeds" 0.890s host=... instance=i-0a1b2c3f
```
dana: can we confirm if this is KV cache pressure or model worker oom? any sudden autoscale activity?
carlos: metrics show steady GPU mem usage on the worker pool but a spike in queue depth around 14:02-14:05. also saw many grpc Unavailable to the model service.
alice: trying a quick mitigation: enabling route fallback to smaller-quantized model variant (latency up, success rate better). applying policy now.
incident-bot: Rollout initiated: route-fallback -> model-quant-small (traffic split 50/50) by alice via console.
ben: good call. i'll watch for regressions on latency. if errors drop we can ramp to 100%.
eve: CS heads up: we're seeing chatter from 2 enterprise customers about brief errors. i'll draft a blurb for status page if this persists > 15m.
carlos: after route split, 5xx rate dropped to 2.3% in the last 60s window. queue depth also easing.
alice: nice. keeping at 50% for 5m to verify. can someone check autoscaler logs for any pending preempt/scale failures?
dana: checking now — no scale failures, but we have a flapping connection between router and a subset of workers (TCP resets). looks like a transient network blip in us-west-2a.
ben: can we cordon the flaky AZ's worker set and drain? that might restore stability fast.
alice: agree. plan: cordon and drain worker-set-usw2a, failover traffic via scheduler to other zones, continue route-fallback. will coordinate with infra.
incident-bot: Action recorded: cordon worker-set-usw2a (alice). ETA 6m.
carlos: logs during the flap show repeated TLS handshake timeouts to instances i-0a1b2c3e/f. infra team notified.
eve: pinging account teams, will let customers know we are mitigation in progress.
ben: status update in 3m unless something changes. holding here. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
alice: cordon + drain started. draining connection pool, migrating in-flight requests.
ben: 2m update — 5xx down to 0.9%, latency +70ms on fallback model but successful responses. traffic routed away from problematic instances.
dana: infra reports the network fabric issue in the AZ flushed after a router reboot on their side. worker instances healthy now.
carlos: switching route-fallback back to primary model variant in 10% increments.
incident-bot: Traffic move scheduled: model-quant-small -> primary in 4 steps (25% every 2m). initiated by carlos.
alice: moving to 75% primary now. monitoring.
ben: all good from my side — error rate stable at 0.4%, latency within SLO.
eve: status page blurb posted: "Partial errors observed in us-west; mitigation in progress; services recovering." linked in #customer-updates.
alice: final check — holding for 5m then close incident if stable. anyone object?
ben: no objections.
carlos: +1
dana: +1
eve: +1 — i'll coordinate post-incident notes for customers.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-4437 moved to monitoring. bridge will remain open for 30m.
alice: closing the thread here once monitoring window passes. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
